case_analysis.thread_summary: This thread covers a complete Bluetooth SIG qualification project for multiple communication terminal products using an existing Bluetooth module and host stack combination. The discussion progresses from initial ICS/profile planning, host stack compatibility analysis, and qualification strategy selection through SIG submission, TCW handling, Product Listing publication, and final compliance folder delivery. The consultant guided the customer through reducing unnecessary testing by reusing existing qualified components and resolving Qualification Workspace consistency issues. The thread also documents operational tasks such as invoice handling, submission review, compliance folder preparation, and future derivative product registration guidance.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The main technical issue involved attempting to combine an existing module QDID with Google Fluoride host stack QDIDs, which triggered Qualification Workspace consistency check Invalid errors related to GAP and GATT ICS dependencies. The consultant determined that the Invalid conditions were caused by internal inconsistencies within Fluoride registrations rather than by the Bluetooth module itself. A Test Case Waiver strategy using an existing Host Subsystem and Controller Subsystem combination was proposed to bypass core-layer Invalid conditions while selectively inheriting existing profile qualifications. The parties evaluated which profiles required new PTS evidence versus which could be inherited from Fluoride 1.5, ultimately deciding to align all profile ICS selections to Fluoride 1.5 and avoid additional HID11 testing. The consultant also clarified representative product handling, allowing one representative model's compliance documentation to cover multiple closely related variants using the same module and host stack.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: The consultant's core reasoning was to minimize new qualification scope by maximizing reuse of existing qualified subsystem registrations and inherited profile evidence while keeping the Qualification Workspace in a valid state. Rather than treating the Invalid errors as module defects, the consultant correctly isolated the issue to newer SIG consistency rules affecting older Fluoride registrations. The strategy therefore shifted from attempting a clean include-only configuration to using a TCW-supported qualification path combined with selective profile inheritance. Additional testing was only justified where inherited ICS coverage could not satisfy the product's required functionality.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: If handled incorrectly, the project could have failed SIG consistency validation and become unregistrable due to unresolved Invalid conditions in the Qualification Workspace. Incorrect interpretation of the GAP/GATT dependency errors could also have led to unnecessary module investigations or unnecessary replacement of the Bluetooth architecture. Over-scoping the qualification effort would have increased PTS testing requirements by forcing new profile evidence generation instead of inheriting existing qualified profiles. Mishandling representative model selection or compliance folder retention requirements could also create audit exposure or future derivative registration problems.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When qualifying products that reuse existing Bluetooth modules and host stacks, the most effective consulting approach is to separate true technical incompatibilities from Qualification Workspace rule inconsistencies, then aggressively reuse existing QDIDs, inherited ICS coverage, and TCW mechanisms to minimize new testing and qualification scope while preserving a valid registration path.
